newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HORSE RACING-CHRONOLOGY OF RECENT HK MISHAPS.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-CHRONOLOGY OF RECENT HK MISHAPS.

text.p: One of the biggest horse-racing scandals to hit Hong Hong began to unfold on Monday.
Following is a chronology of recent mishaps in Hong Kong horse-racing:

March 16/17, 1997 - Hong Kong graft-busting body, Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC), detains 36 people, including a number of jockeys and trainers, after swooping on Shatin racecourse during a probe against alleged illegal bookmaking and race-fixing.
Dec 7, 1996 - Two U.S. race horses withdrawn from race after failing drugs tests.
Oct 30, 1996 - Two Hong Kong jockeys banned from riding for nine months for, racing authorities said, "stopping their horses" in a race at Happy Valley racecourse.
Oct 30, 1996 - Five jockeys end up in hospital after pile-up at Shatin, worst in 26 years of professional racing in Hong Kong.
Sept 18, 1996 - Australian trainer Bruce Hutchison seriously injured in single-vehicle car crash. Surgeons had to rebuild half his face.
April 14, 1996 - Hong Kong Horse of the Year, Makapura Star, destroyed after suffering severe lung haemorrhage in mid-race.

March 25, 1996 - Altogether 20 horses from stable of French trainer Patrick Biancone suspended for seven days after showing traces of drugs. The drug was not performance-enhancing but Hong Kong requires horses to be medication-free seven days before racing.

March 23, 1996 - The HK$2.5 million Gold Cup race at Shatin is thrown into disarray when second favourite Deauville and two other horses are withdrawn from racing after testing positive for Sputolosin, which must be declared when used.
Feb 10, 1996 - Jockey Walter Swinburn, whose successes include the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe and three English Derbies, is seriously injured after fall at start of a race at Shatin racecourse.

Feb 20, 1986 - In the biggest racing scandal on record at the time, the ICAC seizes 22 members of a "Shanghai syndicate", headed by a Shanghainese businessman, subsequently charged with conspiring to dishonestly influence the outcome of six races, involving 75 to 100 horses.
